question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
2 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 3 \cos{(x )}=- 4 y \sin{(x )} + 1\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 3 \cos{(x )}&=- 4 y \sin{(x )} + 1 \\ 2 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 4 y \sin{(x )}&=3 \cos{(x )} + 1 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(2 \sin{(x )})}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{\frac{3 \cos{(x )}}{2} + \frac{1}{2}}_{Q(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=2 \sin{(x )}$ and $Q(x)=\frac{3 \cos{(x )}}{2} + \frac{1}{2}.$

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2 x - y}{x}\,,\ x\ne 0\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{2 x - y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=2 - \frac{y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + \frac{y}{x}&=2 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(\frac{1}{x})}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{2}_{Q(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=\frac{1}{x}$ and $Q(x)=2.$

question.:question/problem:

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y + x^{2} y=x y^{2}\,,\ y\ne 0\,.

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y + x^{2} y&=x y^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y + x^{2} y - x y^{2}&=0 \\ y (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + x^{2} - x y)&=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + x^{2} - x y&=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- x)}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{- x^{2}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- x)}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{- x^{2}}_{Q(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- x$ and $Q(x)=- x^{2}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}}{x^{2}}=\frac{x + y}{x}\,,\ x\ne 0\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

where $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ do not depend on $y.$

We have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}}{x^{2}}&=\frac{x + y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=x^{2} \frac{x + y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=x (x + y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=x^{2} + x y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- x)}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{x^{2}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- x)}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{x^{2}}_{Q(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- x$ and $Q(x)=x^{2}.$
